abstraction_design.rationale: The card/section/badge abstractions are genuinely reused and stretch well, but there is no shared detail-page or partial-refresh abstraction, so a new resource type (Items) is largely copy-paste and CardList is growing a team-specific flag.

findings.issue: Team cookie name, max size and JSON serialization are duplicated between the layout's inline client script and lib/team.ts; changing the format requires editing both in lockstep or the server and browser disagree on the team.
findings.suggestion: Pass the constants in once (e.g. `define:vars` from lib/team.ts, or data attributes) and keep a single canonical encode/decode pair, exporting the same values to the client script.

findings.issue: The layout owns the team add/remove behavior for the whole site: every page ships a delegated handler coupled to data attributes defined in CardList.astro:31 and pokemon/[name].astro:78-81.
findings.suggestion: Move the handler into a small team-specific script co-located with the feature (team.ts or a TeamButton component), so the layout stays generic and removing the team feature touches no shared file.

findings.issue: The resource-detail pattern (fetch by param name, set 404 status, facts <dl>, effect-with-fallback) is copy-pasted across moves, abilities and types pages; a new Items section would copy it a fourth time.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper (e.g. loadResource(kind, name) returning {record, status}) and/or a small ResourceFacts component, so detail pages only declare their specific fields.

findings.issue: Effect fallback chain (englishShortEffect ?? latestEnglishFlavorText ?? DASH) duplicated at abilities/[name].astro:23.
findings.suggestion: Add an `effectText(record)` helper to lib/pokedex.ts next to the two primitives it composes.

findings.issue: The fetch → DOMParser → replaceWith → abort → popstate enhancement is implemented independently (and slightly differently) in index.astro and MovesSection.astro:185-208.
findings.suggestion: Extract one shared 'swap a region from a URL' client helper; both call sites reduce to selectors plus URLs and error behavior stays consistent.

findings.issue: Team-domain logic (getTeamMembers, getTypeCoverage) lives in the generic Pokédex data module, splitting the team feature across six files (team.ts, team.astro, Base.astro, CardList.astro, pokemon page, pokedex.ts).
findings.suggestion: Move both functions into lib/team.ts (importing getTypeLabels/TypeInfo as needed) so the feature has one home.

findings.issue: The `removable` boolean flag puts team-specific markup and semantics inside the shared card component.
findings.suggestion: Use a named <slot slot="actions"> or a per-card action element so CardList stays generic; alternatively accept a render-prop style callback in the team page.

findings.issue: The `note` callback on cardsForPokemon and Card.note exist solely for the abilities page's 'Hidden ability' text, so they become dead code if Abilities is removed.
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is for now, but if the only consumer disappears, delete the param, the Card.note field and .card-note styles in the same change.

summary: A well-organized Astro 7 app: one narrow API seam, one card component, one shared card-list builder that genuinely serves three pages, so removal and data-source changes are close to trivial. The team feature change fits the conventions but leaks into the layout (duplicated cookie code and a global click handler) and adds a flag to CardList. Presentation-level duplication (detail-page skeletons, effect fallback, partial-refresh scripts) is the main thing that will make the next similar page costlier than it should.
